title: 1D dynamic programming
short: Fill a list left to right, each cell built from earlier ones.
what: Make a list where cell i holds the answer for the first i items. Fill it left to right. Each new cell only needs a few cells before it, so one pass gives the answer at the end. The hard part is saying what one cell means.
analogy: Climbing a staircase and writing on each step the best you've done so far. To fill the next step you only look one or two steps back.

frames.label: house robber
frames.say: Rob houses on a street, but never two side by side. best[i] = the most money you can take from houses 0 to i.

frames.label: house robber
frames.say: best[0] = 2: only one house. best[1] = 7: you can't take both 2 and 7, so take the bigger one.

frames.label: house robber
frames.say: House 2: skip it and keep best[1] = 7, or rob it: 9 + best[0] = 11. 11 wins.

frames.label: house robber
frames.say: House 3: skip it (11), or rob it: 3 + best[1] = 10. Skipping wins, so best[3] = 11.

frames.label: house robber
frames.say: House 4: skip it (11), or rob it: 1 + best[2] = 12. Rob it: best[4] = 12.

frames.label: house robber
frames.say: The last cell is the answer: 12, from houses 0, 2 and 4. Each cell used only two cells before it: one pass, O(n).

when: The answer for item i depends on the items before it
Max or min over a sequence with a rule (no two adjacent)
Number of ways to reach step n
python:
def rob(money):
    best = []
    for i, m in enumerate(money):
        take = m + (best[i - 2] if i >= 2 else 0)  # rob house i
        skip = best[i - 1] if i >= 1 else 0          # leave it
        best.append(max(take, skip))
    print(best)
    return best[-1]
print(rob([2, 7, 9, 3, 1]))
watch: Handle the first one or two cells by hand; they have no cells before them.
Say what best[i] means before writing code. Most bugs are a fuzzy meaning.
When a cell only needs the last two, two variables can replace the list.
